root_cause.text: The driver fails to validate the firmware-supplied num_ifs value against the maximum supported interfaces (DPSW_MAX_IF=64), leading to an out-of-bounds write in the fixed-size cfg->if_id array when num_ifs >= 64.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bound check `if (ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs >= DPSW_MAX_IF)` in dpaa2_switch_init(), and the commit description explicitly states that num_ifs controls iteration in dpaa2_switch_fdb_get_flood_cfg() which writes into the array, and that when num_ifs == DPSW_MAX_IF and all ports match, the control interface write overflows by one entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to validate the number of interfaces from firmware against the maximum allowed, preventing out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check that compares ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs with DPSW_MAX_IF and returns -EINVAL with an error message if num_ifs >= DPSW_MAX_IF.
intent_record.how: This prevents the driver from proceeding with initialization if the number of interfaces reported by the firmware exceeds the maximum allowed, avoiding potential out-of-bounds access or undefined behavior.
